Union of India through Defence Estate ...Respondent(s)
Officer Srinagar Through: Mr. T. M. Shamsi, DSGI with Mr. Faizan Ahmad &
 Ms. Yasmeen Jan, Advocates CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR JUSTICE VINOD CHATTERJI KOUL, JUDGE  ORDER 11.07.2024 CM No. 02/2027:
1.
This application filed by applicants/appellants is for amendment of memo of appeal.

2. The Union of India has desired that the land measuring 1477 Kanals and 1  Marlas situated at village Ushkara, Khawajabagh, Khanpora and Gutyar-Baramulla.
be acquired for the defence purposes.
Out of said land, 128 Kanals and 09 Marlas of land was acquired by the J&K State Government, at the instance of Union of India under J&K Land Acquisition Act, in the year 1999/2000.
The Union of India has desired for acquisition of remaining land, i.e., 1348 Kanals and 12  Marlas, under RAIP Act for defence purposes.

The rates offered by the respondents were not acceptable to land owners and, accordingly, Deputy Commissioner, Baramulla, being the competent authority in pursuance of SRO 276 Home..93/79 dated 18.10.95,
appointed the District & Sessions Judge, Baramulla, as arbitrator to make the award in respect of the land measuring 1348 Kanals and 12  Marlas (45 properties) for acquisition under J&K Land Acquisition Act.
Learned District Judge passed the award in the said arbitration proceedings.

sentences.text: The appellants being aggrieved of the award, challenged the same in an appeal.
In the appeal as per the appellants the land acquired under various Survey numbers are not incorporated in the appeal.

It is averred in the application that pursuant to the directions of the Court, the Deputy Commissioner, Baramulla, was asked to provide list of estate holders whose land was acquired for defence purposes.
The Special Collector Defence (Assistant Commissioner, Revenue) Baramulla
, vide communication No. DCB/LRA/2017/84 dated 15.06.2017 provided a detailed list of estate holders as mentioned in para 4 of the application.

It is with respect to these survey numbers that the land is sought to be incorporated by the appellants in the appeal, being part of the total land (1348 Kanlas and 12  Marlas), acquired for the defence purpose and in respect of which award, under challenge, was passed.

4. It is submitted by learned senior counsel for the applicants/appellants that this fact came to the knowledge of the applicants/appellants only when the Deputy Commissioner, Baramulla, mentioned the said survey numbers in its report.
The appellants disputed the amount of compensation and the market value of land which has been acquired.

5. Mr. T. M. Shamsi, learned DSGI objected the amendment on the ground that same cannot be allowed because the claim is time barred and also the appellants could have filed writ petition in respect of land falling survey number mentioned in the application.

6. The arguments made by learned counsel for the respondent do not pass the test of law because the land falling under survey numbers which is sought to be incorporated are part of arbitration proceedings in respect of which award has been passed.
Therefore, applicants/appellants could be permitted to amend the appeal by incorporating said survey numbers.
The contention raised by learned counsel for respondents is, thus, rejected.
7. Application is allowed and amended memo of appeal is taken on record.
CM disposed of.
Mr. T. M. Shamsi, DSGI, prays for and is granted four weeks' time to file supplementary affidavit.

9. List the main matter for final hearing on 01.08.2024.
(VINOD CHATTERJI KOUL) JUDGE SRINAGAR 11.07.2024 Manzoor Ghulam Ahmed Zargar And Ors vs Union Of India Through Defence Estate on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151899407/
